rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, uncertainty is highest and a clean baseline is needed before testing more complex multiprofile, multimodal, or advanced-encoder settings. config_001 tests the simplest RNA-only, single-profile PCA model, establishing an anchor for validation accuracy/F1 and a reference point for later isolating RNA representation, profile/aggregation, and fusion effects. It is the best first experiment because it avoids confounding multiple design choices and efficiently reduces uncertainty about whether added complexity is needed.

The only completed experiment is a sparse baseline: RNA-only, single-profile, PCA with moderate validation accuracy. config_004 keeps modality, profile setting, and aggregation fixed while changing only the RNA encoder from PCA to scvi_n200, directly testing whether a learned RNA representation improves over the simple PCA baseline. This one-factor comparison reduces uncertainty about an important design choice before adding more complex profile, aggregation, image, or fusion decisions, making it an efficient use of the next limited experiment.

Existing evidence shows scvi_n200 singleprofile RNA-only outperforms pca_n2000 in both accuracy and F1, but there is no evidence yet on whether multiprofile representation helps. This experiment tests whether using scvi_n200 with multiple profiles and a simple avgpool aggregation improves over the best singleprofile RNA baseline, clarifying the effect of profile setting/aggregation while keeping the stronger RNA encoder fixed. It is the best next use of budget because it exploits the current promising direction, avoids adding unnecessary complexity such as transformer aggregation or fusion, and reduces uncertainty about a central design choice before investing in more complex multimodal configurations.

The strongest result so far is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) with 0.650 accuracy and 0.628 F1, clearly better than singleprofile scvi_n200. The main remaining uncertainty in this promising branch is whether transformer aggregation improves on avgpool. config_006 keeps model setting, profile setting, and RNA encoder fixed and changes only aggregation, so it isolates the aggregation effect. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the current best direction, is likely to yield high validation performance, and will inform whether avgpool or transformer should be used before testing image fusion.

RNA-only results show that multiprofile scvi_n200 substantially outperforms single-profile scvi_n200 (0.653 vs 0.520 accuracy), while avgpool and transformer aggregation are nearly tied. The key uncertainty is whether this gain is mainly due to multiprofile processing or to the scvi representation. config_003 tests PCA under the same multiprofile/transformer setup as config_006, changing only the RNA encoder. This cleanly isolates the effect of representation and helps decide whether further effort should focus on RNA encoders, aggregation, or moving to image/multimodal models.

Existing RNA-only evidence shows multiprofile scvi_n200 is much stronger than single-profile or PCA transformer, but PCA multiprofile has only been tested with transformer aggregation, leaving uncertainty about whether PCA is inherently weak or whether avgpool aggregation would help. config_002 tests PCA multiprofile with avgpool, directly comparable to config_005 for encoder effects and config_003 for aggregation effects. This is the best next use of budget because it is a low-cost, single-factor comparison that clarifies the RNA representation and aggregation design space before adding image or fusion complexity.

The completed experiments show a strong RNA-only direction: multiprofile with scvi_n200 reaches about 0.65 validation accuracy, while singleprofile RNA is much weaker and PCA is inferior to scvi. However, there is no evidence yet for the image modality, so the key uncertainty is whether image features contain useful signal before investing in multimodal fusion. config_011 tests image-only performance under multiprofile with a standard ResNet50 encoder and simple avgpool aggregation, making it directly comparable to the RNA multiprofile avgpool baseline while avoiding extra confounds from fusion, transformer aggregation, or a larger ViT. This is the best next use of budget because it is a simple, informative exploration of the untested image modality: if image-only is competitive, multimodal extensions become justified; if not, complex multimodal configurations are less attractive.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile scvi_n200 RNA is strong, with avgpool and transformer nearly tied, while image-only resnet50 multiprofile avgpool is much weaker, leaving uncertainty about whether image features are complementary when fused with RNA. config_030 adds resnet50 image features to the strong RNA avgpool baseline using simple concat fusion, keeping profile, RNA encoder, image encoder, and aggregation aligned with existing unimodal baselines. This is the best next experiment because it directly isolates the effect of multimodal fusion with the only tested image encoder, avoiding confounds from untested ViT or transformer aggregation; if it improves over the RNA-only avgpool baseline, image is useful, and if not, resnet image can be deprioritized.

RNA-only scvi_n200 multiprofile models are currently strongest (~0.65 accuracy), while the only tested multimodal configuration (scvi_n200 + resnet50, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) is slightly lower (~0.63), leaving uncertainty about whether concat fusion is limiting the image contribution. config_031 tests weighted fusion while holding model setting, profile setting, RNA encoder, image encoder, and aggregation fixed, so it isolates the effect of fusion. This is the best next experiment because it is a single-factor extension of the most promising multimodal setup and directly clarifies whether fusion can make multimodal profiling competitive with the current RNA-only best.

The strongest evidence is that multiprofile scvi RNA with weighted multimodal fusion is currently best (config_031, acc 0.678), while image-only resnet is weak and the only image encoder tested in multimodal is resnet50. The main uncertainty is whether a stronger image representation, imagenet_vit_l, can improve the weighted multimodal model. config_037 tests this by changing only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while keeping scvi, multiprofile, avgpool, and weighted fusion fixed, making it an efficient exploitation of the best direction and a clean test of image representation.
